title: Sunnyvale
name: Sunnyvale
metaTitle: Sunnyvale 1031 Exchange Investors | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange guidance for Sunnyvale investors evaluating Moffett Park office campuses, Lockheed-adjacent industrial, and Murphy Avenue's downtown redevelopment.

sections.html: Sunnyvale's Moffett Park has spent years turning from AMD's old semiconductor backyard into Google and LinkedIn's Bay Area campuses, and that turnover is still working its way through the leases on nearby buildings. An exchanger who assumes every Moffett Park address carries the same tenant quality as the biggest names nearby is skipping the lease-by-lease review that actually determines the income. The district's next decade will likely be defined by how quickly the remaining AMD- and Lockheed-era buildings either modernize or get replaced, and an exchanger's return depends heavily on which side of that line a given parcel sits.

sections.heading: Moffett Park's Tenant Mix Has Turned Over Faster Than the Skyline
sections.html:
The office and R&D campuses spread across Moffett Park now house Google, LinkedIn, and Amazon alongside older buildings still built for AMD-era semiconductor uses, and the two generations of space don't compete on the same terms. A 1990s R&D shell converted to office use rents differently than a purpose-built campus finished in the last few years.

An exchanger evaluating a Moffett Park building needs to know which generation it belongs to and whether the current tenant's lease reflects that difference, rather than only whether the address sits inside the district's boundary.

sections.heading: Five Product Types in One Zip Code
sections.html:
A workable Sunnyvale shortlist typically spans several product types:

  • large-footprint office and R&D campuses in Moffett Park, leased to major tech tenants
  • older semiconductor-era flex buildings along Mathilda Avenue, priced for conversion or redevelopment
  • Lockheed Martin-adjacent aerospace and defense-use industrial near the Sunnyvale/Mountain View border
  • downtown Murphy Avenue mixed-use retail, riding the walkable-district redevelopment
  • transit-oriented apartments near the Caltrain station

sections.heading: Lockheed's Aerospace Footprint Still Shapes Nearby Industrial
sections.html:
Lockheed Martin's Space division has operated in Sunnyvale for decades, and the surrounding industrial buildings still carry design cues from that use — heavier power capacity, specialized clean-room space, security-driven site layouts.

That specialization is an asset for a similar aerospace or defense tenant and a liability for almost anyone else. A buyer treating this stock as generic industrial without pricing the conversion cost to a standard warehouse use is missing the building's actual re-leasing profile.

sections.heading: The Onizuka Site Shows How Slowly Redevelopment Actually Moves
sections.html:
The former Onizuka Air Force Station, once known locally as the Blue Cube, has moved through redevelopment plans for years, and the pace is a useful reminder that a site's headline potential and its actual delivered timeline are two different things.

An exchanger drawn to a nearby parcel on the promise of a large redevelopment finishing soon should confirm the entitlement status directly with the city rather than pricing the deal on a developer's announced timeline. That same caution applies to any exchanger evaluating a nearby office or industrial parcel marketed on the strength of a redevelopment story rather than its own current lease.

sections.heading: Same File, Same Week, No Exceptions
sections.html:
A Moffett Park or Mathilda Avenue building with a major corporate tenant needs the qualified intermediary, the tax advisor, and a lender who has reviewed the actual lease term and renewal options in the same file before the identification notice goes out.

Wait until the last week and the risk is real: a lender flags tenant concentration, or the lease's renewal option turns out to be less favorable than assumed, and the 180-day window closes with no time to identify a better-underwritten alternative. Confirm details directly with your own tax advisor and qualified intermediary; this page describes the market, not tax advice.

faqs.q: Is a Moffett Park office building automatically a strong 1031 replacement?
faqs.a: Only if its generation of construction and lease terms hold up, since the district mixes older AMD-era shells with newer campuses built for today's tenants.

faqs.q: How should I evaluate Lockheed-adjacent industrial space?
faqs.a: Price the cost of converting specialized aerospace buildout to standard industrial use, since that conversion cost affects both re-leasing speed and resale value.

faqs.q: Can I count on the Onizuka site redevelopment lifting nearby values soon?
faqs.a: Confirm the entitlement status with the city directly. Large redevelopment sites here have a long history of moving slower than initial announcements suggest.

faqs.q: Am I limited to one Moffett Park building for my identification?
faqs.a: No. You can identify up to three properties regardless of value under the standard rule, or more under the 200% rule if combined value stays within twice what you sold.

faqs.q: What if my Sunnyvale identification falls through near Day 45?
faqs.a: Have a real backup ready in a different corridor and avoid touching exchange funds directly while you resolve it.

faqs.q: Does Sunnyvale's downtown Murphy Avenue trade like a corporate submarket?
faqs.a: No. Murphy Avenue draws on walkable, independent retail and restaurant demand tied to downtown redevelopment, a different tenant profile than the large corporate leases that define Moffett Park, so underwrite it on its own foot-traffic terms.

faqs.q: How do I confirm whether a Moffett Park building is older stock or newer construction?
faqs.a: Pull the building's original permit and any renovation history directly. The exterior alone often doesn't reveal which generation of construction, or which lease economics, actually apply to a given address.

faqs.q: Is Caltrain proximity enough to justify a premium on Sunnyvale multifamily?
faqs.a: Verify current walk distance and ridership rather than assuming transit proximity alone, since not every parcel near the corridor sits close enough to the actual station to capture that premium.

faqs.q: Does a large corporate tenant's headquarters status make a Sunnyvale lease safer?
faqs.a: Not on its own. A headquarters designation says nothing about the specific lease term, renewal option, or termination rights on the building you're actually buying, so confirm those terms directly rather than treating the tenant's size as a substitute for underwriting.
